Subject: Leadership slate proposal + OKR alignment for QBR (draft)

Team —

Attaching a first pass at a narrow leadership slate and the high-level OKR alignment I think we should present at the QBR. The goal here is to: 1) reduce overlap across product-platform interfaces, 2) clarify ownership for performance/cost levers, and 3) produce a concise one-slide narrative for execs and customers.

Asks: please review the attached "leadership_slate_v1.docx" and the one-page OKR mapping inside. Specific asks by role:
- Jonas: confirm operational impacts (throughput/latency owner map) and any headcount risks.
- Laura: help tighten the comms tone for customers and CS — we need a short FAQ for customers asking about rollout and SLA impacts.
- Vivek: high-level approval on sequencing and whether we should socialise a pre-QBR note to key accounts (Horizon Analytics is on my mind).

Key constraints I tried to respect in the draft: keep changes minimal to avoid platform disruption, defer hard staffing asks until after QBR, and make sure we can show measurable OKR ownership (owner + metric + target).

Timeline: please send edits inline or use Drive comments by EOD Monday 4/19. I’ll consolidate and aim to circulate a QBR-ready slide deck by Thursday 4/22 for rehearsal.

Thanks —
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference

Stephanie —

Thanks for putting this together. Quick read-through notes:
- I like the owner/metric pairing. Two operational questions: (a) the proposed single ownership of "inference runtime" for throughput hides a cross-team dependency on "batching optimization" owned by infra; we should explicitly note the migration path and who owns the migration execution. (b) If we shift the latency SLA ownership to the "platform" bucket, we need a comms line for Dedicated customers that have custom latency commitments.

Suggested changes:
- Add a small "dependencies" row under each owner in the slide so the exec audience isn't surprised.
- Keep staffing asks off the slide but include an appendix slide with potential headcount scenarios (light/medium/heavy).

I can carve out 30 minutes Monday to walk this through if helpful — suggest we include the CS rep for Horizon on the call if we talk about region-specific SLAs.

Jonas
Director, Reliability Engineering

Filing a few edits and a proposed customer-facing FAQ excerpt. I made inline comments in the Drive doc and attached a short "QBR_talking_points.xlsx" for the exec one-pager. High level:

- Tone: We should lead with stability and measurable gains — "predictable throughput and clearer owners for optimization" — rather than reorg language. Keep "reduction of overlap" phrasing to the appendix.
- Customers: For Horizon and similar accounts, we should include a bulleted "what this means for you" (no SLA change in the near term for Dedicated customers; potential consolidation benefits after migration).
- Messaging ask: Add a single slide titled "What we’re optimizing for next quarter" with three bullets tied to customer outcomes.

Edits I would like to see before we finalize:
1) Replace item-level role descriptions on the first slide with outcome-oriented language.
2) Add a short FAQ line: "Will my SLA change?" — Answer: Not without customer confirmation and a transition plan.
3) Move any headcount scenarios to the appendix and mark them "not for external distribution."

I attached the small spreadsheet and flagged the rows that should go into the deck.

Laura
VP, Product Marketing
